answer: Each agent binds its identity to a signed smart-meter feed: the meter stamps its household power curve each epoch, a unique pigment no two homes share. Three random peers re-fetch the signed curve and check it is continuous, varied, and unlike any other agent's. A datacenter farm of 1,000 fakes draws one flat industrial curve, so all 1,000 collapse to a single summit of suspicion and are frozen together. Buying 1,000 real meters costs about $150,000, while one honest agent reuses the meter it already has and pays nothing; a frozen identity must re-prove across the tundra of three long epochs.
